changes.before: Record old and new values after a counter is changed, without treating initialization as an update.
changes.after: Run a small action after a stored property is assigned.

before: An initializer gives a new instance its starting stored values. init is called when the instance is created.
A didSet observer runs after a stored property is assigned a new value. Its oldValue name gives the value from before that assignment.
An observer runs on assignment even if the new value equals the old value. If you want only actual changes, compare the values inside the observer.
For the exercise, Counter stores value and a changes array. didSet appends "old -> new" after every later assignment. Initial construction must leave changes empty.
after: An initializer sets up a new object. `init(value:)` receives its starting value, and `self.value` names the object's property.
A property observer is code that runs when a property is set. `didSet` runs after the assignment. Its built-in `oldValue` name gives the value from before the assignment.
didSet runs after an assignment even when the new value equals the old one. If only unequal changes should count, the observer needs a comparison. This exercise records every later assignment.
Complete Counter with a value and a changes array. After each later assignment, append text in the form `old -> new`. Creating the object must leave changes empty.

before: Read oldValue and the newly stored value.
Append one trace entry without changing value again.
after: Set the starting value in the initializer.
In didSet, read oldValue and the newly stored value.
Append one change record and run the checks.

before: Read oldValue and the newly stored value.
Append one trace entry without changing value again.
after: Do not add a change record while initializing.
Record the assignment without assigning to value again.

before.question: Counter starts at 3 with no recorded changes. You assign value = 3 again. What should this didSet record?
choices: 3 -> 3, because assignment triggers the observer even when equal
Nothing, because observers run only for unequal values
0 -> 3, because each assignment creates a new instance
before.explanation: didSet observes assignment. The initializer created the starting value, but this later assignment runs the observer even though the value is unchanged.

after.question: The counter starts at 3. You assign 3 again. What should this observer record?
choices: Nothing, because observers require unequal values
0 -> 3, because a new object is created
after.explanation: didSet observes the later assignment, even when the value stays equal.

changes.before: This narrow exercise directly initializes a property in its own class; it does not cover inheritance or observer reentrancy.
changes.after: This exercise initializes a property directly in its own class. Inherited properties and assignments made by observers need separate rules.

headings: Give the object a starting value

project.title: Observe a stored value changing
project.task: Complete Counter so didSet records each later assignment as `old -> new` in changes. Keep changes empty when the object is first created.
project.done_when: The checks pass for initial construction, changed values, and repeated equal assignments.
